card: PeerManager now penalizes peers that send malformed compact blocks during optimistic reconstruction, resolving an existing TODO. When the limit of in-flight compact block reconstructions for a block is reached, additional announcements follow an optimistic path; previously, malformed blocks encountered there were silently ignored while the primary path disconnected the peer. This fixes the behavioral inconsistency and adds test coverage in p2p_compactblocks.py without external dependencies.
changed_since_previous: No functional differences from the earlier version; rebased with test coverage intact.
evidence: Replaces an explicit net_processing TODO ('// TODO: don't ignore failures') added in commit 7017298eb2.
Brings error handling in line with the primary compact block processing path in net_processing, which penalizes peers sending invalid compact block data.
problem: When the maximum number of concurrent in-flight compact blocks for a block is reached, incoming compact block announcements are evaluated via optimistic reconstruction without round-trip transaction requests. If a peer sends a malformed compact block in this path, the node silently drops the message instead of penalizing the peer, which is inconsistent with the primary compact block processing path.

risk.why: Mistakenly treating benign reconstruction failures as malformed data could disconnect honest peers during block propagation.

scope_notes: The net_processing change is two lines; the remainder of the PR is a Python functional test setting up maximum in-flight compact blocks to exercise the optimistic path.
summary: PeerManager now calls `Misbehaving` when `PartiallyDownloadedBlock::InitData` returns `READ_STATUS_INVALID` during optimistic compact block reconstruction. This replaces a TODO comment that previously caused the node to silently ignore all initialization failures in this secondary path.
